scope_caveat: Local optimum over the explicitly tested candidate pool only; not a mathematical or global proof of optimality.

authority.note: PASS covers only the 9 complete configurations in the pool: raw baseline, registry canonical export, preferred five, four-swap keeping Blasphemous Act (no Treachery), the Pass C Stage A six-swap (+Mob Rule -Insurrection), the two Pass C named-cut six-swaps (+Bribery -Thieving Amalgam; +Bribery -Jhoira, Weatherlight Corsair), the five-swap with Dazzling Sphinx instead of Gríma and the Nightveil Specter-over-Locke six-swap. It also covers the named single-card contenders. They were judged with finite current-Oracle rules cases; bounded enumerations answering the Pass C requested measured tests (a 60-cell Mob Rule vs Insurrection grid over five fixed mixed tables, 6/7/8 mana and Don present or removed, with lands-only RR/RRR red availability by 13 cards; Bribery vs Thieving Amalgam and Jhoira over five opponent creature densities counting opponent-owned permanents and opponent turns to the first); exact lands-only colour access; Commander Spellbook combo lookups (0 included combos in both lists); and a quantity-counted mana comparison. Tests run locally and in .github/workflows/m7-don-andres-the-renegade.yml; run URLs are recorded in the PR body. There is no statistical multiplayer ranking, no matched-opening playtest sample, no opponent block/response model and no removal-response rate. The A/B seals and the owner-equivalent Pass C (final disposition KEEP; genuinely independent model NO) are historical, baseline-scoped and not technically independent. Nothing here implies owner approval, M6 certification, M7 approval or a canonical change.
